title: Perfect projection for one constant quotient
statement: With d, f:U→V, n and the fixed finite mate π_n of [def-sp-constant-quotient-projection], assume that each positive quotient A/I^m is perfect over A [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], as recorded in d. For every unbounded K in D(U,A), π_n(K) is an isomorphism in D(V,A). The morphism is the specified counit mate, with no new choice of source or target isomorphisms. There is no completeness, properness, smoothness, etale-origin or boundedness hypothesis on K or f.

proof.text: Choose a bounded finite-projective A-resolution of A/I^(n+1). Exact constant module realization preserves its augmentation quasi-isomorphism and finite-free retractions. Scalar tensor cancellation identifies finite evaluated reduction with total tensor by that resolution on flat K-flat complexes. The reduction counit fixes this comparison; the normalization of reductionPullIso fixes its compatibility with inverse image.

Choose a K-injective representative J of K. Tensor by the bounded finite-projective coefficient preserves K-injectives. The derived-adjunction counit factorization computes the specified finite mate as localization of tensorAdjunctionTotal, through the normalized comparisons from the first step. Finite-free terms give the finite-product projection isomorphism; inclusions and retractions give the finite-projective inverse. Bounded signed totalization gives a chain inverse. Localization preserves both inverse identities, proving invertibility for the one fixed quotient. No tower conservativity is used in this finite theorem.
